abstract: Cell division and cell shape changes drive tissue morphogenesis. Cell division is tightly regulated by biochemical factors that influence the cell cycle. Past work in our lab showed how contractility of mesoderm cells influences cell division orientation during Drosophila gastrulation. Whether contractile forces that drive morphogenetic folding influence the timing of coincident mitotic divisions is unknown. During Drosophila gastrulation, cell division is regulated by mitotic entry of cells in stereotypic regions across the embryo, termed mitotic domains. Here, we examine the role of morphogenesis in the timing of mitotic entry in the mitotic domains. To do this, we disrupted adherens junctions to globally disrupt force transmission across the embryo. In addition, we examined the timing of mitotic entry in mutants that affect mesoderm invagination. Our data suggests a role for mesoderm invagination in mitotic domain 1 timing.
